extracted.intended_audience: law students, faculty, and practitioners researching U.S. administrative law (especially ASU community)
extracted.subtask_description: A library research guide listing treatises, journals, blogs, podcasts, and databases useful for researching federal agencies, administrative procedure, and regulatory issues (including notice-and-comment topics). Emphasizes which secondary sources provide doctrinal overviews, practice tips, histories, and current awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law Treatise (Hickman & Pierce)
rubrics_metrics.description: This three-volume title published by Wolters Kluwer is recognized as the leading treatise in administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance on the administrative law governing a broad variety of topics as well as insight into agency power and procedure. Available on VitalLaw; accessible on campus or remotely with ASURITE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law (Stein et al., Lexis+)
rubrics_metrics.description: This regularly updated treatise, available on Lexis+, provides an analysis of all aspects of administrative law and the administrative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for up-to-date doctrinal analysis; Lexis+ password required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law & Practice (Murphy & Koch, Westlaw)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Law & Practice is a treatise, available on Westlaw, that provides advice, techniques, and tips on the procedures necessary for engaging federal and state agencies in all avenues of regulated conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice-oriented: good for procedural tactics and how-to guidance when interacting with agencies. Westlaw password required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Administrative Procedure Sourcebook
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint online publication by the Administrative Conference of the United States and the ABA Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice; a regularly-updated and annotated compilation of the key legal sources governing nearly every aspect of administrative procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an overview of major laws governing administrative procedure and offers access to statutory text, legislative history, agency regulations, guidance documents, law review articles, and other sources — useful as a starting point for procedural/regulatory legal research. (June 2022 edition noted.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law (hornbook)
rubrics_metrics.description: This hornbook provides a comprehensively updated analysis of administrative law in the United States, placing special emphasis on topics undergoing significant evolution or transformation in the Supreme Court and federal courts of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for authoritative doctrinal overview and courts-focused developments; available on campus or with ASU access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding Administrative Law (study aid)
rubrics_metrics.description: This study aid in the Understanding series is designed to help the reader grasp the fundamental concepts of administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the role of administrative agencies, the process of administrative decision making, and judicial review of agency action — useful for learning foundational concepts and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative & Regulatory Law News (ABA quarterly)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quarterly publication from the ABA's Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice that provides information on developments pertaining to administrative and regulatory law and policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for practitioner-focused updates and developments; available on HeinOnline for ASU users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law Review (journal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Published by American University in conjunction with the ABA Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice; publishes articles by practicing lawyers, judges, and academics, as well as symposia and meetings on current topics in administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly articles and symposia useful for in-depth analysis; available on HeinOnline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Law Review Accord (online companion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The online companion to the Administrative Law Review that publishes content on a rolling basis, including response pieces, student comments, and other shorter scholarly works about the administrative state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for timely shorter pieces and responses that may not appear in the print journal; available on HeinOnline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal of the National Association of Administrative Law Judiciary
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles written by judges, professors, and lawyers on topics specific to developments affecting the administrative judiciary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicially-oriented scholarship useful for perspectives from the administrative judiciary; available on HeinOnline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Michigan Journal of Environmental & Administrative Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes articles, student notes, comments, essays, and online blog posts on all aspects of environmental law, as well as administrative law topics that may apply to environmental law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when administrative law issues intersect with environmental law; available on HeinOnline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yale Journal on Regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishes in-depth scholarly articles twice a year on a range of topics including antitrust, bankruptcy, energy, the environment, financial regulation, health care, information technology, tax, telecommunications, and utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level regulatory scholarship across subject-matter areas; available on HeinOnline.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Administrative Law eJournal (SSRN)
rubrics_metrics.description: An eJournal operated by SSRN that publishes early-stage research articles on administrative law before official publication in academic journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for finding the most up-to-date academic scholarship and early drafts on recent developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harvard Law Review Administrative Law Blog
rubrics_metrics.description: A webpage of the Harvard Law Review that publishes essays, articles, and notes about recent administrative law decisions and issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for short topical essays and timely commentary on recent decisions and issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jotwell: Administrative Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Features abbreviated reviews of recent scholarship, including administrative law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for concise expert summaries and signposts to important recent scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law.com: Administrative Law
rubrics_metrics.description: A Law.com page containing news coverage and analysis of administrative law for legal professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner-oriented news and analysis; useful for current events and practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice & Comment (blog)
rubrics_metrics.description: A blog from the Yale Journal on Regulation and the ABA Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused commentary on regulation and administrative law; useful for accessible practitioner/scholar commentary on notice-and-comment and regulatory issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Regulatory Review
rubrics_metrics.description: An online source of regulatory news, analysis, and opinion housed at the University of Pennsylvania School of Law, published every weekday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features work by law students, scholars, judges, attorneys, and others interested in regulatory developments; useful for daily updates and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Hard Look (podcast)
rubrics_metrics.description: A podcast by the ABA Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice that covers recent events in administrative law, regulatory policy, and critiques and praise of regulations and their efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio resource for discussions of regulatory policy and evaluation of regulations' effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gray Matters (podcast)
rubrics_metrics.description: A podcast of the C. Boyden Gray Center for the Study of the Administrative State that focuses on issues debated around the modern administrative state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for policy-focused conversations and debates about administrative-state issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: HeinOnline: U.S. Federal Agency Documents, Decisions, and Appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: A database featuring reports, decisions, records, and the official case law of the most important U.S. federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary-source collection of agency materials helpful for historical and doctrinal research; available on campus or remotely with ASURITE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lexis+ Practice Area: Administrative Law
rubrics_metrics.description: Lexis+ provides a central location for administrative law materials on its platform through this practice area page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidates cases, administrative codes, administrative decisions, and related resources; Lexis+ password required.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProQuest Regulatory Insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides access to administrative law histories organized by public law number and allows you to locate all regulatory actions associated with a specific CFR part or U.S. Code section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Federal Register documents (1977+) and the Code of Federal Regulations (1991+); useful for tracking regulatory histories and agency rulemaking records. Available on campus or remotely with ASURITE.
